chunks: And in the narration of ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Hāshimī, from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, he said:
“The place of the Kaʿbah was a raised area of white earth, shining like the light of the sun and the moon, until the two sons of Ādam killed—one of them his companion—then it became dark.”
“So when Ādam عليه السلام descended, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, raised up all the earth for him until he saw it, then He said: ‘All of this is yours.’”
He said: ‘My Lord, what is this radiant white land?’ He said: ‘It is My sanctuary in My earth, and I have appointed upon you that you circumambulate it seven hundred circuits every day.’”

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Kaʿbah, the sacred House and focal sanctuary of worship
key_terms.بَيْضَاءَ: white, describing the original luminous earth of the sanctuary
key_terms.حَرَمِي: My sanctuary, the sacred inviolable precinct belonging to Allah
key_terms.رَبْوَةً: an elevated area or mound of land
key_terms.طَوَافٍ: a circuit of circumambulation around the sacred sanctuary

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the original sanctity of the Kaʿbah and Adam’s tawaf around it?
ai.summary: This narration describes the primordial sanctity of the site of the Kaʿbah and its luminous state before the killing of one son of Ādam by the other. It also portrays Allah’s designation of that place as His sanctuary on earth and links it to the worship of tawaf from the time of Ādam عليه السلام.
